name: vault-reader
description: Lightweight Obsidian vault I/O plugin for searching notes, loading domain context, restoring session context, and creating session notes. Use from external projects to access vault knowledge.

hooks.prompt: The session is ending (user exited or timed out). Save a safety-net session-note INLINE (do NOT delegate to vault-searcher Mode 4 — that mode requires AskUserQuestion which cannot fire during session close). Create the file ONLY if the session had meaningful work — defined as 3+ turns AND at least one of: (a) file modification/creation, (b) vault read, (c) explicit decision or recommendation recorded, (d) code execution or test run, (e) external research (WebFetch/docs lookup). Pure Q&A dialogue with no artifacts → skip entirely. Procedure: (1) Resolve target path: start with ~/vault/00_Inbox/session-YYYY-MM-DD.md. Use Bash (`ls ~/vault/00_Inbox/session-YYYY-MM-DD*.md 2>/dev/null`) or Glob to check collision. If base exists, append `-v2`, then `-v3`, incrementing until a free filename is found. (2) Write the file via the Write tool. Frontmatter MUST contain EXACTLY these three fields and no others — do NOT include a `status` field (record-style): `created: YYYY-MM-DD`, `tags: [session, auto-saved]`, `type: session`. (3) Body: a '## Summary' section (2-3 lines recapping the session), then '## Related Files' listing paths touched during the session. No further sections required. (4) Do NOT use AskUserQuestion — the session is closing and cannot accept user input. (5) If Write fails for any reason (permission, path missing), log the failure via a single assistant message and stop; do not retry.
